title: CI/CD Fundamentals
description: Understand the principles of Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment.

data.text: **CI/CD** stands for **Continuous Integration**, **Continuous Delivery**, and **Continuous Deployment**. It is a set of practices that automate the software delivery process — from code commit to production deployment — making releases faster, safer, and more reliable.

terms.definition: Developers merge code changes to a shared branch frequently; each merge triggers an automated build and test.
Every change is automatically built, tested, and prepared for production release — deployments are manual.
Every change that passes all stages is automatically deployed to production — no manual approval.
A chain of automated steps that code changes go through from commit to production.

data.text: A typical CI/CD pipeline consists of several stages. Each stage must pass before the change moves to the next.

data.caption: Stages of a CI/CD pipeline: from code commit through to production deployment.
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Developer pushes code] --> B[Build]
    B --> C[Test]
    C --> D[Lint/Static Analysis]
    D --> E[Build Docker Image]
    E --> F[Push to Registry]
    F --> G[Deploy to Staging]
    G --> H[Acceptance Tests]
    H --> I{Manual Approval?}
    I -->|Yes| J[Deploy to Production]
    I -->|No - CD| J

items: **Source** — Code is committed to a version control system (e.g., Git).
**Build** — The code is compiled and packaged into an artifact.
**Test** — Unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end tests run automatically.
**Analyze** — Static analysis, linting, and security scanning check code quality.
**Package & Publish** — The application is containerized and pushed to a registry.
**Deploy** — The application is deployed to staging and then production.

data.title: A sample CI/CD pipeline definition
data.content: This is what a CI/CD pipeline looks like as code — versioned alongside your application.
data.code:
name: CI Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build

cards.title: Manual Deployment
cards.description: A human builds, tests, and deploys each release by hand.
pros: Full human control at every step

cards.title: CI/CD Pipeline
cards.description: Automated testing and deployment on every code change.

items: **Faster time to market** — Ship features and fixes quickly.
**Lower risk** — Small, frequent changes are easier to debug.
**Improved quality** — Tests catch bugs before they reach users.
**Reliability** — Automated deployments are reproducible and reversible.
**Developer productivity** — Less time spent on manual builds and deployments.

data.title: CI/CD maturity levels
data.text: Level 1: No CI/CD. Level 2: Automated builds and tests. Level 3: Automated deployments to staging. Level 4: Automated production deployments with rollback. Level 5: Full continuous deployment.

data.title: Evaluate your CI/CD readiness
data.description: Assess where your current deployment process stands.
steps: Map out your current deployment process from commit to production.
Identify manual steps that could be automated.
Count how many times you deploy per week.
List common failure points in your current process.
Identify which CI/CD stages would have the biggest impact.
data.expectedOutcome: A clear understanding of your CI/CD maturity and a plan for incremental improvement.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CI/CD automates the path from code commit to production deployment.
Continuous Integration = frequent merges with automated builds and tests.
Continuous Deployment = every passing change goes to production automatically.
CI/CD reduces risk, speeds up delivery, and improves software quality.
data.takeaway: CI/CD transforms software delivery from a scary, manual event into a smooth, automated flow.
